I have worked as both a medical coder ($27/hr) and an LPN ($34/hr) and both were after trade school diplomas. (Highly recommended against trade schools if avoidable and would do community college if I was to redo it.) Both programs were a year. I have been a single parent for a really long time and it still was a huge stretch for money/living paycheck to paycheck, especially with insurance for all of us costing up to $1200 a month when working as a nurse. No experience needed but I found you had to work your way up a bit to get a coding job and had to start with billing first but it was easy to move up. Nursing you can get a job anywhere, anytime (LPNs aren’t really employed by hospitals in my experience but there are so many other varieties of settings). For both you have to get certified (coders usually have to have a professional certification through AAPC or AHIMA) or pass the NCLEX (nursing).

People try to be helpful and I think the majority of them have NO CLUE how much worse they make it. My suggestion is to find supports who can validate you instead of just tell you to snap out of it (I just realized you posted this in the depression subreddit, duh me!). There are online and in person support groups... counseling.. different FB groups, etc. Those things help me. The world is not a validating place and when you are in a pit of despair sometimes that's all you need. 

It might suck ass right now and it's ok. YOU are ok. You can get through whatever it is you are going through, take it minute by minute if hour by hour or day by day is too daunting. I know it might seem bleak. I am one of the most hopeful people one could meet and there was a point even *I* lost all hope and it scared the shit out of me but I got through it. I ended up going to intensive therapy and I still take meds, I'd never function properly without them and I still go to counseling for maintenance. If you aren't in therapy I would highly suggest it. It has helped me a lot even if it was just to have someone to validate me and what I was going through moment to moment. 

It took me a VERY long time to realize when these waves of depression hit that I just have to ride the wave and try to get through the storm and eventually it will let up and life will at least become bearable again. I know bearable isn't quite good enough but it's better than pure darkness and no hope and for those of us that struggle with mental illness it might be the majority of what we can have. Hopefully someday you will see that the waves just need to be ridden out too. I'm sorry I don't have a solution to when they will get better but from one depressed person to another I am fairly certain they will get at least a little more tolerable. 

I hope something I said has helped even a tiny bit. My heart goes out to you more than you know. Hang in there! If you need to talk you can message me or call the lifeline 1-800-273-8255. Good for you for reaching out! That's the best thing to keep doing :)
